chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said:

A man said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and I was listening, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I frequently make mistakes in the prayer.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'And has anyone ever been safe from it?' So he said, 'I do not think anyone makes more mistakes than me.' So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'O Abu Muhammad! The servant, a third of his prayer is raised for him, and half of it, and three-quarters of it, and less and more, according to the measure of his omission therein, but it is completed for him from the optional prayers.' He said, so Abu Baseer said to him, 'I do not see that the optional prayers should be left in any state.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, it should not.'
ai.seo_question: How is the validity of prayer determined when a person makes frequent mistakes during recitation?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while the reward for obligatory prayer is graded according to the frequency of mistakes—ranging from one-third to full acceptance—this partial validity is distinct from the perfection achieved through the accumulation of voluntary (Nawafil) prayers. This hadith underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the compensatory role of Nawafil, ensuring that the believer's worship remains complete and spiritually robust despite human fallibility.

en.hubeali: And frm him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘A man said to Abu Abdullahasws, and I heard, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! I frequently make mistakes in the Salāt’. So heasws said: ‘And has there anyone ever been safe from it?’ So he said, ‘I don’t think anyone would have more mistakes than me’. So Abu Abdullahasws said to him: ‘O Abu Muhammad! The servant, there is Raised for him a third of his Salāt, and a half of it, and three-quarters of it, and less, and more, upon a measurement of his omission therein, but it is completed for him (when he offers) the optional (Salāt)’. So Abu Baseer said to himasws, ‘I do not see that the optional (Salāt) should be left upon any state’. So heasws said: ‘Yes, it should not’.
en.sarwar: 3. It is a narration from him (narrator of previous Hadith) by Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn abu Hamzah from abu Basir from who has said the following:

“Once, when I was present, a man said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, I make a great number of mistakes in my Salah (prayer).’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Has anyone remained safe thereby?’ I (the narrator) then said, ‘I think no one makes as many mistakes as I do.’ Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, then said to him, ‘O abu Muhammad, sometimes of Salah (prayer) of a servant (of Allah) one-third is raised, sometimes one-half or three- fourth or less or more depending upon the quantity of one’s mistakes in that Salah (prayer). However, it is completed with his optional Salah (prayer).’ Abu Basir then said to him (the Imam), ‘I think, optional Salah (prayer) should not be omitted in any condition.’ Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, then said, ‘Yes, it should not be omitted.’”
